items.problem: A stored unit (a turn, a fact, a chunk) is retrieved and read out of its context. Pronouns, ellipsis, deictic time ('last week', 'there') and elided speakers make the unit ambiguous or unmatched by the query, so the unit is either not found (lexical or embedding mismatch) or found but misread. The generic fix is to make each retrieval unit self-contained at write time, or to carry context into the unit at embed time.

items.problem: Reported scores are not comparable: different judges, different category sets (cat 5 often dropped), different answer models, different retrieval budgets, and different data cuts. A system comparison needs the protocol next to the number.

evidence.method: heuristic: counts are LoCoMo class sizes from docs/v2/LOCOMO_PROBLEM_MAP.md; no question ids listed here. Detail: Gaps A4, A10, A12, A13, I2, I14-I16. Our reference: 81.4% on cat 1-4 (1,540 questions) with a local 9B reader and judge; question-sampling CI +-2.2 points.

items.existing: Built. Suite fixed by the owner (LoCoMo + cat 5, OP-Bench, MAB-CR, ConvoMem, PrefEval; no LongMemEval), adoption rule average-led. Gaps: cat 5 unmeasured (I2), A4 official judge, I14 gold audit for non-LoCoMo sets, I15 splits.

hypothesis.statement: Reporting each system with (judge, category set, reader, retrieval budget, CI) in one table, plus our run under the official judge prompt, removes the apparent gaps between systems that come from protocol.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Not a score effect; reduces the spread of published numbers to the CI.

hypothesis.statement: Cat 5 results should be reported as a separate abstention metric (A13): precision of refusals and answer rate on answerable items.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Makes I1/I3 trade-off visible; headline accuracy on cat 1-4 unchanged.

solutions.name: LoCoMo
solutions.generic_mechanism: 10 very long dialogues (about 300 turns, 9K tokens avg per the paper, up to 35 sessions), QA categories single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, adversarial; event-summarisation and multimodal tasks.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Original paper: long-context and RAG LLMs lag humans by a wide margin, especially on temporal reasoning. Systems commonly report cat 1-4 only.

solutions.name: LongMemEval
solutions.generic_mechanism: 500 questions over scalable chat histories with five abilities (extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, abstention).
solutions.cost: Public; excluded from our suite by owner decision.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Commercial assistants and long-context LLMs drop sharply (about 30-60% accuracy drop reported); proposes session decomposition, fact-augmented keys and time-aware query expansion.

solutions.name: LoCoMo-Plus
solutions.generic_mechanism: Adds cue-trigger 'cognitive' items where the link between cue and trigger is implicit.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Memory systems score about 10-26% on the cognitive part while scoring higher on factual LoCoMo (e.g. Mem0 57.24 LoCoMo avg vs 15.80 cognitive per our research note).

solutions.name: MemoryAgentBench
solutions.generic_mechanism: Four competencies: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, conflict resolution, built from incremental multi-turn interactions.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: No tested method masters all four; conflict resolution is weakest.

solutions.name: PrefEval
solutions.generic_mechanism: Preference following over long, inserted-conversation contexts; explicit, implicit, and persona forms.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Reported that preference following degrades with context length for many LLMs (figures not re-checked).

solutions.name: OP-Bench
solutions.generic_mechanism: Over-personalisation: irrelevant, baiting, repetition, and memory-sycophancy cases.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Memory systems lower the average versus no-memory (BASE 73.8 vs Mem0 42.12, MemU 35.09, MemOS 37.17 with Qwen3-8B per our SOTA note).

solutions.name: ConvoMem
solutions.generic_mechanism: Early-conversation memory benchmark; argues the first 150 conversations do not need RAG.
solutions.risk: see reported_effect and cost; limits not separately scored
solutions.reported_effect: Full-context beats memory systems at small history size.

top10.technique: Sufficiency-gated answer / infer / abstain policy (Sufficient Context, Chain-of-Note, CRAG idea)
top10.why: The only cat 5 lever, and cat 5 is 446 questions never measured; LIB-12 gate and LIB-43 deep tier already exist, so the cost is wiring plus one screen.

top10.technique: One targeted second retrieval that names the missing slot (IRCoT / Self-Ask idea, bounded)
top10.why: List/count/join questions are the largest wrong family with a retrieval cause; B8 says lost gold is in sessions with no hit.

top10.technique: Deterministic date calculator for the reader (PoT/PAL idea without code execution)
top10.why: 10 plus 1 questions are pure arithmetic; zero model cost; rule-only and safe.

top10.technique: Session or episode gist leg lifted to turns (ReadAgent / SeCom / RAPTOR idea)
top10.why: Targets the 68 stage-b recall misses; all pieces exist flag-off (S31, S33, S61).

top10.technique: Hits-first evidence ordering and edge placement (Lost in the Middle / Found in the Middle)
top10.why: Free, addresses the largest single class (`wrong_detail` 46); already a setting, no screen.

top10.technique: Deterministic pre-judge plus a second-family judge for agreement
top10.why: Protects every other measured gain from judge error in both directions; cheap.

top10.technique: Document expansion at write (generated questions per fact, filtered), not query-time HyDE
top10.why: Pays at write once, avoids the query-time harm that Weller et al. and our B14 found; can share the extraction call.

top10.technique: Reranker over a wider pool plus protected family pool; test convex combination vs RRF
top10.why: Targets 47 cut-stage losses; the retrieval-only screens are free.

top10.technique: Rule-built context prefix on embedded text; late chunking as a later step
top10.why: Gets a share of the contextual-retrieval gain with no LLM call; moderate integration risk.

top10.technique: Event-time supersede with value histories verified on a knowledge-update slice
top10.why: Little LoCoMo effect but the core claim of a memory engine; MAB-CR is the proxy since LongMemEval is out of the suite.
